claim: A patent holder need not demonstrate actual lost sales to establish damages where the infringing party systematically incorporated protected process claims into its production line; the Federal Circuit held that reasonable royalty calculations may be anchored to the defendant's own internal cost-savings projections derived from use of the patented method.
citation: Wrothbury v. Cascade Forge Manufacturing Inc., 687 F.2d 1142 (Fed. Cir. 2009)
initial_reasoning: Wrothbury v. Cascade Forge Manufacturing Inc. (Fed. Cir. 2009) addressed the calculation of damages for patent infringement but held that a plaintiff must establish actual loss or use the plaintiff’s own cost‑savings projections only when the defendant’s use of the patented method is proven. It does not support the claim that a patent holder need not demonstrate lost sales and that reasonable royalty may be anchored solely to the defendant’s internal cost‑savings projections.
